Dataset-level version of `Fig4.effect-size-comparison-flu-sc2glu.Rmd`. Instead of the
integrated fluconazole and sc2glu datasets, each dataset is its own condition and concordance
is tested for every pair: YPD.1, YPD.2 and sc2glu.1, sc2glu.2 (replicates of the two
baselines) and fluconazole at two doses, Flu.1 = 16 ug/ml (`Flu.1_16ug`) and
Flu.2 = 8 ug/ml (`Flu.2_8ug`). The two doses are not replicates and are never merged, so
Flu.1 vs Flu.2 is a dose comparison.

**Direction matters.** A comparison "A vs B" takes the *significant* eQTLs of A
(condition 1) and looks up the same variant-gene pair among *all tested* variants of B
(condition 2, the `first_assoc` files). B vs A starts from B's significant eQTLs instead, so
the two directions give different totals, found/not-found counts and concordance. Every
ordered pair (both directions) is computed; `cond1_name` / `cond2_name` themselves are only
labels.

**What "concordant" / "discordant" mean.** Concordance is defined per eQTL, i.e. per
variant-gene pair, and the gene is always the same in both conditions (the lookup joins on
Gene + SNP + Variant_Type). For each significant eQTL of condition 1:

- *Cond1-only*: the same variant-gene pair is not present in condition 2's `first_assoc` file
  (not tested there; this is NOT the same as "not significant in condition 2").
- *Shared-Concordant*: the pair is present in condition 2 and the effect has the same sign,
  `sign(Beta_Cond1) == sign(Beta_Cond2)`: the variant changes that gene's expression in the
  same direction in both datasets.
- *Shared-Discordant*: present in condition 2 but with the opposite sign.

"Shared" only means the pair was tested in condition 2; no significance cutoff is applied to
`P_Cond2`. Gene-level lists are derived from these eQTL labels afterwards (see the
categorization and concordant-genes sections).

**What this chunk does:** Sets knitr chunk options, loads the libraries (tidyverse, data.table, clusterProfiler, org.Sc.sgd.db, ...) and pins `select`, `filter`, `count`, `first` and `bind_rows` to dplyr, since other loaded packages mask them.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
source("/projects/rps/cgsb/gresham/Akriti/wildyeast1/common_analysis_for_all/Agrawal_single_cell_eqtl_cell_cycle/shared_code/arial_font.R")  # Arial for all plots, as in Figs 2 and 5
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Sc.sgd.db)
library(enrichplot)
library(stringr)
library(parallel)

# resolve masking
bind_rows <- dplyr::bind_rows

first     <- dplyr::first
```

# STEP 1: Conditions and file locations

All datasets use the same genotype files and GWAS settings as Figure.4:
SNPs and InDels from the 96-strain MAF15 runs (`--double-id`), CNVs and SVs from the
new PLINK files. YPD.1's InDel run sits in a differently named folder (same
`indels.96samples` file).

**What this chunk does:** Defines where every dataset's results live. `make_cond()` builds, for one condition, the paths to the four significant-eQTL files (SNPs, CNVs, InDels, SVs) and the four per-gene GWAS result folders. `CONDS` lists the six datasets (YPD.1 uses a differently named InDel folder/file). `PAIRS` holds every ordered pair of conditions (6 x 5 = 30): cond1 = the condition whose significant eQTLs are tested, cond2 = the condition they are looked up in. `REP_PAIR` picks the one pair drawn in the single-pair figures. The chunk also creates the output folder, reads the core count from SLURM, and stops if any input file or folder is missing.

```{r config}
ROOT <- "/projects/rps/cgsb/gresham/Akriti/wildyeast1/common_analysis_for_all"

SNP_DIR   <- "results_SNPs_96_MAF15_from_969_strains_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5"
INDEL_DIR <- "results_Indels_96_MAF15_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5"
CNV_DIR   <- "results_CNVs_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_no_chr17"   # CNV GWAS re-run without chr17
SV_DIR    <- "results_SVs_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files"

make_cond <- function(res, tag, indel_dir = INDEL_DIR,
                      indel_file = paste0("all_signif_Indels_", tag, "_96_MAF15_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_with_threshold.txt")) {
  res <- file.path(ROOT, res)
  list(
    signif = c(
      SNPs   = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_SNPs_", tag, "_96_MAF15_from_969_strains_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_with_threshold.txt")),
      CNVs   = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_CNV_", tag, "_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_no_chr17_with_threshold.txt")),
      InDels = file.path(res, indel_file),
      SVs    = file.path(res, paste0("all_signif_SVs_", tag, "_with_double_id_is_not_needed_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_run_from_new_plink_files_with_threshold.txt"))),
    dirs = c(
      SNPs   = file.path(res, SNP_DIR),
      CNVs   = file.path(res, CNV_DIR),
      InDels = file.path(res, indel_dir),
      SVs    = file.path(res, SV_DIR)))
}

CONDS <- list(
  YPD.1    = make_cond("YPD.1/fastlmm/results", "YPD.1",
                       indel_dir  = "results_Indels_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5",
                       indel_file = "all_signif_Indels_YPD.1_with_double_id_final_filtered_for_ncount_less_than_5_with_threshold.txt"),
  YPD.2    = make_cond("YPD.2/fastlmm/results", "YPD.2"),
  sc2glu.1 = make_cond("sc2glu.1/fastlmm_sc2.glu.1_only/results", "sc2glu.1_only"),
  sc2glu.2 = make_cond("sc2glu.2/fastlmm_sc2.glu.2_only/results", "sc2glu.2_only"),
  Flu.1_16ug = make_cond("Flu.1/fastlmm/results", "Flu.1"),   # fluconazole 16 ug/ml
  Flu.2_8ug  = make_cond("Flu.2/fastlmm/results", "Flu.2")    # fluconazole 8 ug/ml
)
COND_NAMES <- names(CONDS)
VARIANTS   <- c("SNPs", "CNVs", "InDels", "SVs")

# every ordered pair (cond1 = significant set, cond2 = lookup)
PAIRS <- expand.grid(cond1 = COND_NAMES, cond2 = COND_NAMES, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(cond1 != cond2) %>%
  mutate(cond1 = factor(cond1, COND_NAMES), cond2 = factor(cond2, COND_NAMES)) %>%
  arrange(cond1, cond2) %>%
  mutate(cond1 = as.character(cond1), cond2 = as.character(cond2),
         comparison = paste(cond1, "vs", cond2))

# the pair shown in the single-pair figures
REP_PAIR <- c("YPD.1", "Flu.1_16ug")

OUTPUT_DIR <- "../results/replicates_concordance"
dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

N_CORES <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK", "8"))

# fail early on a missing input
missing <- c(unlist(lapply(CONDS, `[[`, "signif")), unlist(lapply(CONDS, `[[`, "dirs")))
missing <- missing[!file.exists(missing)]
if (length(missing)) stop("Missing inputs:\n", paste(missing, collapse = "\n"))
cat("Conditions:", paste(COND_NAMES, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Ordered pairs:", nrow(PAIRS), "\n")
```

# STEP 2: Load significant eQTLs (all variant types combined)

**What this chunk does:** Reads the significant eQTLs of each condition for all four variant types and stacks them into one table per condition (`signif_combined`), tagging each row with `Variant_Type`. Prints a table of how many significant eQTLs each condition has per variant type.

```{r load-data}
read_signif <- function(path) {
  fread(path, sep = "\t", quote = "", data.table = FALSE)
}

signif_combined <- lapply(CONDS, function(cfg) {
  bind_rows(lapply(VARIANTS, function(vt)
    read_signif(cfg$signif[[vt]]) %>% mutate(Variant_Type = vt)))
})

signif_counts <- bind_rows(lapply(COND_NAMES, function(cn)
  signif_combined[[cn]] %>% count(Variant_Type) %>% mutate(Condition = cn))) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Variant_Type, values_from = n) %>%
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(any_of(VARIANTS)), na.rm = TRUE))
print(signif_counts)
```

# STEP 3: Look up every significant variant-gene pair in every other condition

For each condition B and each gene, B's `first_assoc` file is read once, keeping every
variant that is significant for that gene in *any* other condition. Each ordered pair A vs
B is then a join of A's significant eQTLs with this table (same result as reading B's file
separately for every A). Cached to `lookup_<B>.rds`.

**What this chunk does:** For each condition B, collects every variant-gene pair that is significant in at least one *other* condition, then reads B's per-gene `first_assoc.txt` file (all tested variants for that gene) once per gene x variant type, in parallel, and keeps only those variants. The result (`lookups[[B]]`) holds B's effect size (`SnpWeight`) and p-value for every pair any other condition might ask about. Each table is cached as `lookup_<B>.rds`; delete the cache files to force a rebuild.

```{r build-lookup}
read_first_assoc <- function(path, snps) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  d <- tryCatch(fread(path, sep = "\t", select = c("SNP", "SnpWeight", "PValue"),
                      showProgress = FALSE),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
  d[SNP %in% snps]
}

build_lookup <- function(condB) {
  cache <- file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("lookup_", condB, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(cache)) return(readRDS(cache))

  # variant-gene pairs significant in any other condition
  wanted <- bind_rows(lapply(setdiff(COND_NAMES, condB), function(cn)
    signif_combined[[cn]] %>% select(Gene = Source_Phenotype, SNP, Variant_Type))) %>%
    distinct()
  jobs <- wanted %>% group_by(Variant_Type, Gene) %>%
    summarise(snps = list(unique(SNP)), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("%s: %d gene x variant-type files to read\n", condB, nrow(jobs)))

  res <- mclapply(seq_len(nrow(jobs)), function(i) {
    vt <- jobs$Variant_Type[i]; g <- jobs$Gene[i]
    d <- read_first_assoc(file.path(CONDS[[condB]]$dirs[[vt]], g, paste0(g, ".first_assoc.txt")),
                          jobs$snps[[i]])
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0) return(NULL)
    d[, `:=`(Gene = g, Variant_Type = vt)]
    d
  }, mc.cores = N_CORES)
  lookup <- rbindlist(res) %>% as.data.frame() %>%
    distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type, .keep_all = TRUE)
  saveRDS(lookup, cache)
  lookup
}

lookups <- lapply(setNames(COND_NAMES, COND_NAMES), build_lookup)
sapply(lookups, nrow)
```

**What this chunk does:** For every ordered pair (A vs B), joins A's significant eQTLs with B's lookup table on Gene + SNP + Variant_Type. Only pairs present in both survive (inner join). Each row then carries `Beta_Cond1`/`P_Cond1` (A, significant) and `Beta_Cond2`/`P_Cond2` (B, any p-value). The 30 tables are saved to `concordance_all_pairs.rds` and the number of found eQTLs per pair is printed.

```{r retrieve-concordance}
retrieve_pair <- function(cond1, cond2) {
  signif_combined[[cond1]] %>%
    select(Gene = Source_Phenotype, SNP, Variant_Type, Beta_Cond1 = SnpWeight, P_Cond1 = PValue) %>%
    distinct(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    inner_join(lookups[[cond2]] %>% select(Gene, SNP, Variant_Type,
                                           Beta_Cond2 = SnpWeight, P_Cond2 = PValue),
               by = c("Gene", "SNP", "Variant_Type")) %>%
    mutate(Condition1 = cond1, Condition2 = cond2)
}

conc <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PAIRS)), function(i)
  retrieve_pair(PAIRS$cond1[i], PAIRS$cond2[i])), PAIRS$comparison)

saveRDS(conc, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "concordance_all_pairs.rds"))
sapply(conc, nrow)
```

# STEP 4: Concordance statistics for every pair

**What this chunk does:** For every pair, computes: how many of A's significant eQTLs were found / not found in B; how many found eQTLs are concordant (same sign of beta) vs discordant; Pearson and Spearman correlation of A vs B betas; a one-sided binomial test of whether sign concordance exceeds 50%; and a resampling null (B's betas shuffled with replacement, 5000 times) for sign concordance and Pearson r, giving empirical p-values. Writes `Concordance_summary_all_pairs.csv` (one row per pair) and `Concordance_by_variant_type_all_pairs.csv` (the same numbers split by SNPs/CNVs/InDels/SVs).

```{r concordance-stats}
set.seed(42)

calculate_concordance_stats <- function(concordance_data, cond1_total, comparison_name,
                                        n_perms = 5000) {
  n_retrieved  <- nrow(concordance_data)
  n_not_found  <- cond1_total - n_retrieved
  directions   <- sign(concordance_data$Beta_Cond1) == sign(concordance_data$Beta_Cond2)
  n_concordant <- sum(directions, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_discordant <- n_retrieved - n_concordant
  obs_sign_conc <- n_concordant / n_retrieved

  obs_r   <- cor(concordance_data$Beta_Cond1, concordance_data$Beta_Cond2, method = "pearson")
  obs_rho <- cor(concordance_data$Beta_Cond1, concordance_data$Beta_Cond2, method = "spearman")

  binom_result <- binom.test(n_concordant, n_retrieved, p = 0.5, alternative = "greater")

  # resampling null (cond2 effects resampled with replacement, as in the original analysis)
  perm_sign <- replicate(n_perms, {
    perm_beta2 <- concordance_data$Beta_Cond2[sample(n_retrieved, n_retrieved, replace = TRUE)]
    sum(sign(concordance_data$Beta_Cond1) == sign(perm_beta2), na.rm = TRUE) / n_retrieved
  })
  perm_r <- replicate(n_perms, {
    perm_beta2 <- concordance_data$Beta_Cond2[sample(n_retrieved, n_retrieved, replace = TRUE)]
    cor(concordance_data$Beta_Cond1, perm_beta2, method = "pearson")
  })

  list(data = concordance_data, comparison = comparison_name,
       cond1_total = cond1_total, n_not_found = n_not_found, n_retrieved = n_retrieved,
       n_concordant = n_concordant, n_discordant = n_discordant,
       obs_sign_conc = obs_sign_conc, obs_r = obs_r, obs_rho = obs_rho,
       perm_sign = perm_sign, perm_r = perm_r,
       perm_p_sign = sum(perm_sign >= obs_sign_conc) / n_perms,
       perm_p_r = sum(perm_r >= obs_r) / n_perms,
       binom_result = binom_result, n_total = n_retrieved)
}

conc_stats <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PAIRS)), function(i) {
  calculate_concordance_stats(conc[[i]],
                              cond1_total = nrow(signif_combined[[PAIRS$cond1[i]]]),
                              comparison_name = PAIRS$comparison[i])
}), PAIRS$comparison)

summary_table <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PAIRS)), function(i) {
  s <- conc_stats[[i]]
  data.frame(Condition1 = PAIRS$cond1[i], Condition2 = PAIRS$cond2[i],
             Comparison = PAIRS$comparison[i],
             Total_Cond1_eQTLs = s$cond1_total,
             Cond1_only = s$n_not_found,
             Cond1_only_Pct = round(100 * s$n_not_found / s$cond1_total, 1),
             Found_in_Cond2 = s$n_retrieved,
             Found_Pct = round(100 * s$n_retrieved / s$cond1_total, 1),
             Concordant = s$n_concordant,
             Concordant_Pct = round(100 * s$obs_sign_conc, 1),
             Discordant = s$n_discordant,
             Pearson_r = round(s$obs_r, 4), Spearman_rho = round(s$obs_rho, 4),
             Binomial_p = signif(s$binom_result$p.value, 3),
             Perm_p_sign = s$perm_p_sign, Perm_p_r = s$perm_p_r)
}))
print(summary_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(summary_table, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Concordance_summary_all_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

variant_breakdown <- bind_rows(lapply(conc, function(d)
  d %>% group_by(Condition1, Condition2, Variant_Type) %>%
    summarise(N_eQTLs = n(),
              Concordant = sum(sign(Beta_Cond1) == sign(Beta_Cond2)),
              Concordant_Pct = round(100 * Concordant / N_eQTLs, 2),
              Pearson_r = if (n() > 2) round(cor(Beta_Cond1, Beta_Cond2), 4) else NA_real_,
              Spearman_rho = if (n() > 2) round(cor(Beta_Cond1, Beta_Cond2, method = "spearman"), 4) else NA_real_,
              .groups = "drop")))
write.csv(variant_breakdown, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Concordance_by_variant_type_all_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Concordance across all pairs

**What this chunk does:** Draws three heatmaps side by side, one tile per ordered pair (x = condition 1, y = condition 2): % of condition-1 eQTLs found in condition 2, % of found eQTLs that are sign-concordant, and the Pearson r of effect sizes. Saved as `Fig_concordance_heatmaps_all_pairs.tiff`.

```{r concordance-heatmaps, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
heat <- summary_table %>%
  mutate(Condition1 = factor(Condition1, COND_NAMES), Condition2 = factor(Condition2, rev(COND_NAMES)))

h_found <- ggplot(heat, aes(Condition1, Condition2, fill = Found_Pct)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", Found_Pct)), size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2C7FB8", name = "% found") +
  labs(title = "Cond1 eQTLs found in Cond2", x = "Condition 1 (significant)", y = "Condition 2 (lookup)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

h_conc <- ggplot(heat, aes(Condition1, Condition2, fill = Concordant_Pct)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", Concordant_Pct)), size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#27AE60", name = "% concordant") +
  labs(title = "Sign concordance of found eQTLs", x = "Condition 1 (significant)", y = "Condition 2 (lookup)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

h_r <- ggplot(heat, aes(Condition1, Condition2, fill = Pearson_r)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Pearson_r)), size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#E74C3C", mid = "white", high = "#8E44AD", midpoint = 0, name = "Pearson r") +
  labs(title = "Effect-size correlation", x = "Condition 1 (significant)", y = "Condition 2 (lookup)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

conc_heat <- gridExtra::arrangeGrob(h_found, h_conc, h_r, nrow = 1)
grid::grid.draw(conc_heat)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Fig_concordance_heatmaps_all_pairs.tiff"), conc_heat,
       width = 18, height = 5.5, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw")
```

# STEP 5: Effect size plot (one pair)

**What this chunk does:** For `REP_PAIR` only: scatter plot of each found eQTL's effect size in condition 1 (x) against condition 2 (y). Points are green if concordant and red if discordant; one linear fit line per variant type, labelled on the line; dashed 1:1 line; a box with Pearson r, Spearman rho, % sign concordance and n. Saved as `Fig_effect_size_concordance_<pair>.tiff`.

```{r effect-size-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
rep_name <- paste(REP_PAIR[1], "vs", REP_PAIR[2])

make_concordance_plot_by_variant <- function(conc_data, stats, comparison_label, xlab, ylab) {
  variant_colors <- c("SNPs" = "#3498DB", "CNVs" = "#E67E22", "InDels" = "#9B59B6", "SVs" = "#E74C3C")
  plot_data <- conc_data %>%
    mutate(direction = ifelse(sign(Beta_Cond1) == sign(Beta_Cond2), "Concordant", "Discordant"))

  x_range <- range(plot_data$Beta_Cond1, na.rm = TRUE)
  x_width <- diff(x_range)
  label_positions <- data.frame(Variant_Type = VARIANTS,
                                x_pos = x_range[1] + c(0.15, 0.35, 0.55, 0.75) * x_width,
                                y_pos = NA_real_)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(label_positions))) {
    sub <- plot_data %>% filter(Variant_Type == label_positions$Variant_Type[i])
    if (nrow(sub) > 1) {
      fit <- lm(Beta_Cond2 ~ Beta_Cond1, data = sub)
      label_positions$y_pos[i] <- predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(Beta_Cond1 = label_positions$x_pos[i]))
    }
  }
  label_positions <- label_positions %>% filter(!is.na(y_pos))

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(Beta_Cond1, Beta_Cond2)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = direction), size = 2, alpha = 0.3) +
    # one regression line per variant type (types with < 2 shared eQTLs are skipped)
    lapply(intersect(VARIANTS, names(which(table(plot_data$Variant_Type) > 1))), function(vt)
      geom_smooth(data = plot_data %>% filter(Variant_Type == vt),
                  method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = variant_colors[[vt]], linewidth = 1.2)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_label(data = label_positions,
               aes(x = x_pos, y = y_pos, label = Variant_Type, color = Variant_Type),
               size = 4.2, fontface = "bold", fill = alpha("white", 0.7), label.size = 0,
               show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Concordant" = "#27AE60", "Discordant" = "#E74C3C", variant_colors),
                       breaks = c("Concordant", "Discordant"), name = "Direction") +
    annotate("label", x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2,
             label = sprintf("Pearson r = %.3f\nSpearman rho = %.3f\nSign concordance = %.1f%%\nn = %d",
                             stats$obs_r, stats$obs_rho, 100 * stats$obs_sign_conc, stats$n_total),
             size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", fill = alpha("white", 0.85)) +
    labs(title = comparison_label,
         x = bquote("Effect size " * beta * " (" * .(xlab) * ", significant)"),
         y = bquote("Effect size " * beta * " (" * .(ylab) * ")"),
         subtitle = "Points: colored by concordance | Lines & labels: variant type | Dashed: 1:1") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0.5),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey60"),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey95", linewidth = 0.2))
}

p_rep <- make_concordance_plot_by_variant(conc[[rep_name]], conc_stats[[rep_name]], rep_name,
                                          REP_PAIR[1], REP_PAIR[2])
print(p_rep)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("Fig_effect_size_concordance_", REP_PAIR[1], "_vs_", REP_PAIR[2], ".tiff")),
       p_rep, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw")
```

# STEP 6: Null distribution plot (one pair)

**What this chunk does:** For `REP_PAIR` only: histograms of the resampled null distributions from the statistics chunk, for sign concordance (left) and Pearson r (right). The coloured vertical line is the observed value, the dashed line the no-agreement expectation (0.5 and 0); labels give the binomial and resampling p-values. Saved as `Fig_null_distribution_<pair>.tiff`.

```{r null-distribution-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=5}
make_null_plot_combined <- function(stats) {
  perm_df <- data.frame(sign_conc = stats$perm_sign, pearson_r = stats$perm_r)
  p_sign <- ggplot(perm_df, aes(sign_conc)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey70", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = stats$obs_sign_conc, color = "#E74C3C", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
    annotate("label", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.4, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
             label = sprintf("Observed = %.3f\nbinomial p = %.2e", stats$obs_sign_conc, stats$binom_result$p.value)) +
    labs(title = "Sign concordance distribution", x = "Sign concordance (resampled)", y = "Frequency") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
  p_r <- ggplot(perm_df, aes(pearson_r)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey70", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = stats$obs_r, color = "#27AE60", linewidth = 1.2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
    annotate("label", x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.4, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
             label = sprintf("Observed = %.3f\np-value = %.4f", stats$obs_r, stats$perm_p_r)) +
    labs(title = "Pearson r distribution", x = "Pearson r (resampled)", y = "Frequency") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
  gridExtra::arrangeGrob(p_sign, p_r, nrow = 1, top = stats$comparison)
}

p_null_rep <- make_null_plot_combined(conc_stats[[rep_name]])
grid::grid.draw(p_null_rep)
ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("Fig_null_distribution_", REP_PAIR[1], "_vs_", REP_PAIR[2], ".tiff")),
       p_null_rep, width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 600, compression = "lzw")
```

# Analysis: Categorization and gene sets (all pairs)

Each significant condition-1 eQTL (variant-gene pair) is labelled Cond1-only,
Shared-Concordant or Shared-Discordant as defined at the top. Gene sets are then:

- `shared_concordant`: genes with >= 1 concordant eQTL (same variant, same gene, same sign).
- `shared_discordant`: genes with >= 1 discordant eQTL (same variant, same gene, opposite sign).
- `cond1_only_eqtl_genes`: genes with >= 1 eQTL not found in condition 2.

These sets overlap: a gene with several variants can be in more than one of them (e.g. one
concordant and one discordant variant). `cond1_only_egenes` / `cond2_only_egenes` are
different: genes significant (with any variant) in one condition but not the other.

**What this chunk does:** For every pair, labels each of condition 1's significant eQTLs as Cond1-only (not found in condition 2), Shared-Concordant or Shared-Discordant (left join of all condition-1 eQTLs to the found ones). Counts and percentages per category per pair are written to `eQTL_sharing_categories_all_pairs.csv`.

```{r categorize-eqtls}
categorize_eqtls <- function(signif_data_cond1, concordance_data, cond1_name) {
  all_sig_cond1 <- signif_data_cond1 %>%
    select(SNP, Gene = Source_Phenotype, Beta_Cond1 = SnpWeight, Variant_Type, P_Cond1 = PValue) %>%
    distinct(SNP, Gene, Variant_Type, .keep_all = TRUE)
  found <- concordance_data %>% select(SNP, Gene, Variant_Type, Beta_Cond2, P_Cond2)
  all_sig_cond1 %>%
    left_join(found, by = c("SNP", "Gene", "Variant_Type")) %>%
    mutate(Found_in_both = !is.na(Beta_Cond2),
           Direction_Match = ifelse(Found_in_both, sign(Beta_Cond1) == sign(Beta_Cond2), NA),
           # generic labels so every pair plots on the same axis
           Category = case_when(!Found_in_both ~ "Cond1-only",
                                Direction_Match ~ "Shared-Concordant",
                                TRUE ~ "Shared-Discordant"))
}

eqtl_categories <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PAIRS)), function(i)
  categorize_eqtls(signif_combined[[PAIRS$cond1[i]]], conc[[i]], PAIRS$cond1[i]) %>%
    mutate(Condition1 = PAIRS$cond1[i], Condition2 = PAIRS$cond2[i], Comparison = PAIRS$comparison[i])),
  PAIRS$comparison)

category_counts <- bind_rows(eqtl_categories) %>%
  count(Comparison, Condition1, Condition2, Category) %>%
  group_by(Comparison) %>% mutate(Pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>% ungroup()
write.csv(category_counts, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "eQTL_sharing_categories_all_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

**What this chunk does:** Turns the eQTL labels into gene lists for every pair: genes with at least one Cond1-only, Shared-Concordant or Shared-Discordant eQTL, plus eGenes significant only in condition 1 or only in condition 2. All lists are written in long format to `Gene_sets_all_pairs.csv`, and the size of each list per pair is printed.

```{r extract-genes}
extract_category_genes <- function(categorized_data, signif_cond2) {
  genes_cond1 <- unique(categorized_data$Gene)
  genes_cond2 <- unique(signif_cond2$Source_Phenotype)
  list(
    cond1_only_eqtl_genes = categorized_data %>% filter(Category == "Cond1-only") %>% pull(Gene) %>% unique(),
    shared_concordant     = categorized_data %>% filter(Category == "Shared-Concordant") %>% pull(Gene) %>% unique(),
    shared_discordant     = categorized_data %>% filter(Category == "Shared-Discordant") %>% pull(Gene) %>% unique(),
    # eGenes significant in one condition but not the other
    cond1_only_egenes     = setdiff(genes_cond1, genes_cond2),
    cond2_only_egenes     = setdiff(genes_cond2, genes_cond1))
}

gene_sets <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PAIRS)), function(i)
  extract_category_genes(eqtl_categories[[i]], signif_combined[[PAIRS$cond2[i]]])), PAIRS$comparison)

gene_sets_long <- bind_rows(lapply(names(gene_sets), function(cmp)
  bind_rows(lapply(names(gene_sets[[cmp]]), function(set)
    tibble(Comparison = cmp, Gene_set = set, Gene = gene_sets[[cmp]][[set]])))))
write.csv(gene_sets_long, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Gene_sets_all_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

gene_set_sizes <- gene_sets_long %>% count(Comparison, Gene_set) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gene_set, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
print(gene_set_sizes, n = Inf)
```

# Concordant genes (all pairs), with plots for all pairs combined and one pair

Gene-level concordance of effect *size*, not only direction. Only the concordant eQTLs
(same sign in both conditions) are kept and grouped by gene. For genes with >= 3 such
variants, Pearson r is computed between Beta_Cond1 and Beta_Cond2 across those variants;
`|r| > 0.5` = "High concordance". Genes with < 3 concordant variants have r = NA and fall
into "Low concordance / < 3 variants". Note that `abs(r)` is used, so a strong negative
correlation also counts as high.

**What this chunk does:** For every pair, keeps only concordant eQTLs, groups them by gene and records the number of variants, mean |beta| in each condition and (for >= 3 variants) the Pearson r between the two conditions' betas. Genes with |r| > 0.5 are flagged as high concordance. Writes the per-gene table (`Gene_concordance_stats_all_pairs.csv`) and a per-pair count of high vs low genes (`Concordant_genes_summary_all_pairs.csv`).

```{r go-prep}
prepare_concordant_genes <- function(conc_data, min_effect_size_corr = 0.5) {
  concordant_vars <- conc_data %>%
    filter(sign(Beta_Cond1) == sign(Beta_Cond2), abs(Beta_Cond1) > 0, abs(Beta_Cond2) > 0)
  gene_concordance <- concordant_vars %>%
    group_by(Gene) %>%
    summarise(N_variants = n(),
              Mean_abs_beta_cond1 = mean(abs(Beta_Cond1)),
              Mean_abs_beta_cond2 = mean(abs(Beta_Cond2)),
              Pearson_r = if (n() > 2) cor(Beta_Cond1, Beta_Cond2) else NA_real_,
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(Has_high_correlation = !is.na(Pearson_r) & abs(Pearson_r) > min_effect_size_corr)
  list(genes_high_concordance = gene_concordance %>% filter(Has_high_correlation) %>% pull(Gene),
       genes_low_concordance  = gene_concordance %>% filter(!Has_high_correlation) %>% pull(Gene),
       gene_concordance_stats = gene_concordance)
}

go_prep <- setNames(lapply(conc, prepare_concordant_genes), PAIRS$comparison)

gene_concordance_all <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PAIRS)), function(i)
  go_prep[[i]]$gene_concordance_stats %>%
    mutate(Condition1 = PAIRS$cond1[i], Condition2 = PAIRS$cond2[i], Comparison = PAIRS$comparison[i])))
write.csv(gene_concordance_all, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Gene_concordance_stats_all_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

concordance_gene_summary <- gene_concordance_all %>%
  mutate(Category = ifelse(Has_high_correlation, "High concordance (|r| > 0.5)",
                           "Low concordance / < 3 variants")) %>%
  group_by(Comparison, Condition1, Condition2, Category) %>%
  summarise(N_Genes = n(), Mean_Effect_Size_Corr = mean(Pearson_r, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
print(concordance_gene_summary, n = Inf)
write.csv(concordance_gene_summary, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "Concordant_genes_summary_all_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

**What this chunk does:** Stacked bar chart, for all pairs, of how many genes with concordant eQTLs are high concordance (|r| > 0.5) vs low concordance or with fewer than 3 variants. Saved as `Fig_concordant_genes_all_pairs.tiff`.

**What this chunk does:** For `REP_PAIR` only: histogram of the per-gene Pearson r (genes with >= 3 concordant variants), with dashed lines at -0.5 and 0.5 and the |r| > 0.5 genes in green. Saved as `Fig_concordant_genes_<pair>.tiff`.

# GO enrichment (three-way, one pair)

Gene categories for every pair are in `Gene_sets_all_pairs.csv`; the GO dotplot is drawn for
`REP_PAIR`.

"Shared (high concordance)" here is defined differently from the section above: the gene
must be an eGene (significant with any variant) in *both* conditions, and Pearson r is
computed over *all* its found variants, concordant and discordant, requiring >= 3 variants
and `|r| > 0.5`. Because discordant variants are included and `abs(r)` is used, a gene
with consistently reversed effects (strong negative r) is also counted here.

**What this chunk does:** Reads the gene universe (all protein-coding genes in the custom annotation). For every pair, splits eGenes into condition-1-only, condition-2-only and shared (significant in both), and among shared genes keeps those with |r| > 0.5 across all their found variants; gene counts per category are written to `GO_gene_categories_summary_all_pairs.csv`. For `REP_PAIR` only, runs GO enrichment (`enrichGO`, all ontologies, BH-adjusted, lists with < 10 genes skipped) on the three lists and, if at least two give significant terms, draws a combined dotplot saved as `GO_<pair>_three_way.tiff`.

```{r go-enrichment, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
tested_universe <- read.csv("/scratch/aa9679/SingleCell_cerevisiae/Gene_exp_analysis/yeast_custom_annotations.csv") %>%
  filter(gene_biotype == "protein_coding") %>% pull(gene_id) %>% unique()

prepare_three_way_categories <- function(concordance_data, all_signif_cond1, all_signif_cond2,
                                         min_effect_size_corr = 0.5) {
  genes_cond1  <- unique(all_signif_cond1$Source_Phenotype)
  genes_cond2  <- unique(all_signif_cond2$Source_Phenotype)
  genes_shared <- intersect(genes_cond1, genes_cond2)
  high <- concordance_data %>% filter(Gene %in% genes_shared) %>%
    group_by(Gene) %>%
    summarise(Pearson_r = if (n() > 2) cor(Beta_Cond1, Beta_Cond2) else NA_real_, .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Pearson_r), abs(Pearson_r) > min_effect_size_corr) %>% pull(Gene)
  list(cond1_only = setdiff(genes_cond1, genes_cond2), high_conc_shared = high,
       cond2_only = setdiff(genes_cond2, genes_cond1), all_shared = genes_shared)
}

three_way_all <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(nrow(PAIRS)), function(i)
  prepare_three_way_categories(conc[[i]], signif_combined[[PAIRS$cond1[i]]],
                               signif_combined[[PAIRS$cond2[i]]])), PAIRS$comparison)
go_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(three_way_all), function(cmp)
  tibble(Comparison = cmp,
         Category = c("Cond2-only", "High concordance shared", "Cond1-only"),
         N_Genes = c(length(three_way_all[[cmp]]$cond2_only), length(three_way_all[[cmp]]$high_conc_shared),
                     length(three_way_all[[cmp]]$cond1_only)))))
write.csv(go_summary, file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, "GO_gene_categories_summary_all_pairs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

run_enrichGO <- function(gene_list, label, universe, ontology = "ALL") {
  g <- intersect(gene_list, universe)
  cat(sprintf("  %s | genes in universe: %d\n", gsub("\n", " ", label), length(g)))
  if (length(g) < 10) { cat("    -> too few genes (<10), skipping\n"); return(NULL) }
  res <- enrichGO(gene = g, universe = universe, OrgDb = org.Sc.sgd.db, keyType = "ORF",
                  ont = ontology, pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 0.05, qvalueCutoff = 0.1)
  if (is.null(res) || nrow(res) == 0) { cat("    -> no significant terms\n"); return(NULL) }
  cat(sprintf("    -> significant terms: %d\n", nrow(res)))
  res
}

tw <- three_way_all[[rep_name]]
go_lists <- setNames(list(tw$cond2_only, tw$high_conc_shared, tw$cond1_only),
                     c(paste0(REP_PAIR[2], "-only"), "Shared\n(high concordance)", paste0(REP_PAIR[1], "-only")))
print(sapply(go_lists, length))
go_res <- lapply(names(go_lists), function(g) run_enrichGO(go_lists[[g]], g, tested_universe)) %>%
  setNames(names(go_lists))
go_res <- go_res[!sapply(go_res, is.null)]

if (length(go_res) >= 2) {
  cg <- merge_result(go_res)
  cg@compareClusterResult$Cluster <- factor(cg@compareClusterResult$Cluster, levels = names(go_lists))
  cg@compareClusterResult$Description <- str_wrap(cg@compareClusterResult$Description, width = 60)
  p_go <- dotplot(cg, showCategory = 15) + ggtitle(paste("GO enrichment:", rep_name)) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8, color = "black", lineheight = 0.85),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "black", angle = 30, hjust = 1),
          axis.title.y = element_blank())
  print(p_go)
  n_terms <- length(unique(p_go$data$Description))
  ggsave(file.path(OUTPUT_DIR, paste0("GO_", REP_PAIR[1], "_vs_", REP_PAIR[2], "_three_way.tiff")), p_go,
         width = 12, height = max(7, 0.35 * n_terms + 2), units = "in", dpi = 300,
         device = "tiff", compression = "lzw", limitsize = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("Fewer than 2 categories with significant GO terms; dotplot skipped.\n")
}
```
